title: Ubisoft Requires AI Plans in Project Pitches or Opt-Out
summary: Ubisoft now mandates that new project pitches explain planned generative AI use or justify opting out, according to anonymous employee reports.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Ubisoft now requires all new project pitches to detail planned generative AI integration or provide written justification for not using AI technology.
- Anonymous employees report the policy took effect in November 2026, marking a shift toward mandatory AI consideration in game development workflows.
- Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney publicly endorsed the approach, signaling broader industry momentum toward AI integration in creative production pipelines.


Ubisoft has implemented a new internal policy requiring all project pitches to include detailed plans for generative AI integration or provide written justification for opting out, according to anonymous employees who spoke to multiple outlets this week. The policy, officially launched on November 27, 2026, represents one of the most explicit AI mandates from a major game publisher to date.


## New Pitch Requirements


Under the new framework, developers submitting project proposals must dedicate a section to explaining how they plan to leverage generative AI tools throughout the production pipeline. Teams choosing not to incorporate AI technology must submit formal documentation explaining their rationale. The policy applies to all new pitches across Ubisoft's global studios, affecting hundreds of potential projects in various stages of conceptual development.


Anonymous sources describe the mandate as a significant shift from previous guidelines, which treated AI adoption as optional. The requirement now places the burden of proof on teams that prefer traditional workflows, effectively inverting the decision-making hierarchy around AI tools in creative production.


## Industry Reaction and Tim Sweeney Endorsement


Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney publicly endorsed Ubisoft's approach on social media, calling it a pragmatic response to evolving production economics. Sweeney's support signals broader industry momentum toward mandatory AI consideration, particularly among publishers facing rising development costs and extended production timelines. His comments sparked debate within game development communities, with some praising efficiency gains and others raising concerns about creative autonomy.


The endorsement from a competing publisher suggests the policy may become a template for other major studios evaluating their own AI governance frameworks.


## Availability and Implementation Timeline


Officially launched on November 27, 2026, the policy is now active across all Ubisoft studios worldwide. Internal communications reviewed by sources indicate the company expects full compliance within the current fiscal quarter, with training sessions scheduled for creative directors and production leads throughout December 2026.


## Implications for Creative Workflows


The mandate raises questions about how creative teams will balance AI tool adoption with artistic vision. Potential applications include:


- Procedural environment generation for open-world titles
- Dialogue and quest branching assistance for narrative designers
- Concept art iteration and style exploration for visual development
- Localization acceleration across multiple language markets


However, the opt-out provision acknowledges that certain project types, particularly those with strict art direction requirements or legacy franchise constraints, may benefit from traditional workflows.


## What This Means


Ubisoft's policy represents a turning point in how major publishers approach AI governance. By making AI consideration mandatory rather than optional, the company is forcing internal teams to actively engage with generative tools or articulate why alternatives serve their creative goals better. This framework could become standard across the gaming industry, fundamentally reshaping how studios evaluate and greenlight new projects. The policy's success or failure will likely influence similar decisions at other major publishers navigating the intersection of creative integrity and technological efficiency in 2026 and beyond.
